headline: Risk curator integrating with existing protocols; limited contract ownership, primarily operates as strategy manager and risk parameter setter

findings.text: Clearstar is a risk curation service (not a DeFi protocol in traditional sense) that integrates with lending protocols (Morpho, Euler, Upshift, HypurrFi) to manage vault strategies and set risk parameters. No name-tagged contracts on Etherscan under 'Clearstar' protocol label; addresses are embedded in website vault links.

Website pages (clearstar-vaults.html, execution.html) describe three active vault deployments: (1) Morpho USDC vault on Ethereum, (2) Flare FXRP vault via Upshift at 0x373D7d201C8134D4a2f7b5c63560da217e3dEA28, (3) HypurrFi risk curation role. No centralized deployments document found at /docs/deployments or similar paths.
No audit links provided in per-protocol context; audit_links field is empty. No audit reports discovered in fetched website or GitHub repositories.

GitHub organization (Clearstar-Labs) contains 3 repositories: portfolio_tooling (Python), spectra-pt-oracle-deployer (Solidity fork), euler-labels-Clearstar (JavaScript fork for curation whitelist). No Foundry broadcasts or hardhat-deploy artifacts indicating Clearstar-owned protocol deployments. Repos are primarily tooling and integrations.

Eleven chains listed in protocol.chains: Flare, Ethereum, Base, Hyperliquid L1, Hemi, Starknet, Monad, Arbitrum, Katana, Unichain, Polygon. Evidence found for Flare (Upshift vault) and Hyperliquid (HypurrFi) integrations. Ethereum Morpho vault confirmed on website. Other chain deployments mentioned in abstract or external sources (Starknet Vesu, Base activity from Mantapex) but not yet linked to specific curated contract addresses discoverable from pinned sources.

Clearstar acts as curator/risk manager for existing lending protocol vaults, not operator of factory contracts. No factory enumeration required; discovered vaults are direct integrations with third-party vault systems (Morpho, Upshift, HypurrFi, Euler, Spectra).

Discovered address roles: Upshift vault 0x373D7d201C8134D4a2f7b5c63560da217e3dEA28 (vault, Flare), HypurrFi haHYPE contract 0xAc207FFa0bfcE194Db18D1820902D48a2d948968 (collateral asset monitored, Hyperliquid). Clearstar holds curator/risk-manager role, not smart contract ownership.

Addresses 0x373D7d201C8134D4a2f7b5c63560da217e3dEA28 and 0xAc207FFa0bfcE194Db18D1820902D48a2d948968 cited from website vault deployment descriptions (clearstar-vaults.html). No separate Clearstar protocol smart contracts confirmed as in-scope; Clearstar operates as off-chain risk curator and parameter setter.

rationale.verdict: Clearstar is a risk curation and vault strategy management service that does not deploy core smart contracts; it operates as a curator role within third-party protocols (Morpho, Upshift, HypurrFi, Euler, Spectra) across 11 chains. Limited on-chain contract ownership/control; primary function is off-chain risk analysis and on-chain parameter/vault configuration within permissioned curator roles granted by host protocols. Discovered vault addresses and some integration points, but comprehensive address enumeration across all 11 chains incomplete due to fetch-tool budget exhaustion and lack of centralized deployment index. Grade is 'unknown' because the protocol's control model (curator role grants by third-party protocols rather than owned smart contracts) does not fit traditional discovery categorization; subsequent slices (control, autonomy, ability-to-exit) will need to assess whether curator grants constitute meaningful governance/control surfaces or are limited to parameter-setting within host-protocol constraints.

evidence.shows: Protocol website describes Clearstar as risk curator building enterprise-grade infrastructure and strategies. Mentions 'every strategy undergoes rigorous vetting' and 'active on-chain protection.' Lists three active vaults across Ethereum, Flare, and Hyperliquid.

GitHub organization with 3 public repositories: portfolio_tooling (Python), spectra-pt-oracle-deployer (Solidity fork), euler-labels-Clearstar (JavaScript fork for Euler curation whitelist). No primary protocol contracts; primarily tooling and integration repos.

Details three active vault deployments: (1) 'High Yield USDC' on Ethereum/Morpho; (2) 'Flare XRP Vault' on Flare via Upshift at address 0x373D7d201C8134D4a2f7b5c63560da217e3dEA28; (3) 'HypurrFi Integration' on Hyperliquid with haHYPE collateral at 0xAc207FFa0bfcE194Db18D1820902D48a2d948968. Clarifies that Clearstar acts as curator and does not custody funds. $120M+ TVL across 3 active vaults.

Deep technical document describing Clearstar's execution governance posture: control surfaces, permissions, oracle management, liquidity realism, monitoring loops, and response pathways for curated deployments. Defines Clearstar's role as setting enforceable constraints and managing risk within host-protocol frameworks; emphasizes non-custody model and rules-based governance.

Tweet confirms Clearstar strategies manage $120M deployed capital with zero loss events, supported by monitoring and automated response systems. Details XRP/Flare integration: 'XRPL signature → FXRP minting → vault allocation → on-chain strategies' via Xaman wallet and Flare Smart Accounts.

Confirms Clearstar's Starknet deployment: launching pool on Vesu (lending protocol) with Noon Capital's sUSN yield-bearing stablecoin as collateral. Clearstar brings risk management and operations expertise; targets sophisticated strategies. Dated February 2026, confirms active multi-chain operations.

Third-party tracker (Mantapex) reports Clearstar as Risk Curator category with $128.87M TVL across 10 chains: Flare ($60.75M), Ethereum ($50.07M), Base ($8.43M), Hyperliquid L1 ($5.72M), Arbitrum, Starknet, Hemi, Katana, Unichain, Polygon. Data snapshot as of May 2026.

unknowns: D1-offchain: Block explorer name-tag search not attempted for all 11 chains due to fetch-tool budget exhaustion. Specific contract addresses on Base, Arbitrum, Hemi, Monad, Katana, Unichain, Polygon not yet discovered from pinned sources.

D2-offchain: No canonical 'Deployed Contracts' or 'Addresses' documentation page found at protocol.website or docs subdomain. Vault information scattered across strategy pages (clearstar-vaults.html) and app integrations (Morpho, Upshift, HypurrFi links).

D3-offchain: audit_links empty in per-protocol context; no audit reports discovered in fetched sources. Unknown whether Clearstar's risk frameworks, vault contracts, or integrations have been formally audited.

D4-offchain: GitHub repo analysis incomplete. spectra-pt-oracle-deployer and euler-labels-Clearstar are forks; no inspection of commit SHAs or broadcast artifacts performed due to fetch-tool constraints. portfolio_tooling (Python) has no discoverable deployment addresses.

D5-offchain: Only 3 of 11 chains (Flare, Ethereum, Hyperliquid) have specific vault addresses discovered from pinned sources. Remaining chains (Base, Arbitrum, Starknet, Hemi, Monad, Katana, Unichain, Polygon) either have activity per Mantapex TVL data but no pinned contract addresses, or have zero surfaced deployments from available sources.
D6: Not applicable—Clearstar does not operate factory contracts; it integrates with existing vault and lending protocol factories.

D7-offchain: Role taxonomy incomplete. Upshift vault (0x373D7d201C8134D4a2f7b5c63560da217e3dEA28) labeled 'vault' but Clearstar's specific actor role (curator, risk-setter, operator) not fully characterized from fetched HTML. HypurrFi haHYPE (0xAc207FFa0bfcE194Db18D1820902D48a2d948968) is the collateral asset itself, not a Clearstar-controlled contract; Clearstar sets LTV and risk parameters.

D8-offchain: No on-chain read API fetches attempted for discovered addresses due to budget exhaustion. Cannot verify Clearstar administrative control, proxy admin status, or ownership of 0x373D7d201C8134D4a2f7b5c63560da217e3dEA28 and 0xAc207FFa0bfcE194Db18D1820902D48a2d948968 from live contract state.

protocol_metadata.about: Clearstar is a risk curator that builds enterprise-grade vault strategies and risk management infrastructure across decentralized lending protocols. Rather than operating its own smart contracts, Clearstar functions as a curator and parameter-setter within existing protocols (Morpho, Euler, Upshift, HypurrFi, Spectra) to manage vaults, set risk parameters, and deploy capital across DeFi markets on behalf of depositors. The platform emphasizes qualitative-first risk analysis, non-custodial capital deployment, and continuous on-chain monitoring with predefined response pathways for stress conditions.
